_comment: Hand-maintained facts the POM metadata cannot express, merged into
overrides  - a dependency whose POM <licenses> block is absent, empty or wrong.
elections  - a dual/multi-licensed dependency, recording which licence we take.
proprietary - components that are NOT open source; listed for completeness
because they ship in the APK, but they carry no OSS grant.
embedded   - upstream projects vendored INSIDE a dependency's own native
library. They are not separate artifacts, so no classpath or
crate scan can reach them, but their code ships all the same.
vendored   - upstream projects whose SOURCE is copied into THIS repository and
built here rather than consumed as a published artifact. Also
invisible to a classpath scan, but the obligation is wider: we
redistribute their source and may have modified it, so each entry
records the path and whether it was changed.
Keys are Maven coordinates WITHOUT the version (embedded and vendored entries are
keyed on a project name instead, having no coordinate), so a version bump does not
silently drop the entry. The task fails the build if an override no longer
matches anything on the classpath, so stale entries surface instead of rotting.

net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android.note: The published POM carries a <licenses> entry with a URL but an EMPTY <name>, so automated tooling reports no licence for it. SQLCipher Community Edition is BSD-3-Clause, copyright ZETETIC LLC. It embeds SQLite, which its authors released into the public domain.

net.java.dev.jna:jna.note: JNA has been dual-licensed since version 4.0: a recipient may use it under either the LGPL 2.1 (or later) or the Apache License 2.0. Pingolin Note elects Apache-2.0, so no LGPL obligation attaches to this distribution. JNA is a genuine runtime dependency, not just a test one - the UniFFI-generated Kotlin bindings call the Rust .so through it, and it is declared as `implementation("net.java.dev.jna:jna:5.18.1@aar")` in library/build.gradle.kts.

com.google.android.gms.note: Google Play services client libraries. Proprietary; redistributed under the Android SDK licence terms, not an OSS licence.

com.google.android.play:core-common.license: Play Core Software Development Kit Terms of Service

com.google.android.play:integrity.license: Play Integrity API Terms of Service
com.google.android.play:integrity.note: Proprietary Google component used for device attestation.

SQLite.note: SQLCipher is a fork of SQLite. Its authors dedicated it to the public domain: 'The author disclaims copyright to this source code.'

OpenSSL.note: SQLCipher links OpenSSL statically for its cryptographic primitives; the exact build is identified by the version banner inside the shipped binary ('OpenSSL 3.0.16 11 Feb 2025'). OpenSSL 3.x is Apache-2.0.

_spdx_aliases_comment: POM <licenses><name> is free text, so the same licence arrives under half a
dozen spellings ('Apache 2.0', 'The Apache Software License, Version 2.0', ...).
Mapping them onto SPDX identifiers is what lets the summary count a licence
once and lets every row link to the licence text. Cargo already emits SPDX,
so this only ever needs to grow for JVM dependencies.
